root_cause.text: In the Intel DG NVM driver probe function, the `nvm->nregions` field was initialized after the loop that populated the `nvm->regions` array, so any access to the array (e.g., `nvm->regions[n]`) occurred while `nregions` was still uninitialized (zero), causing an out-of-bounds access when the region count was later used.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `nvm->nregions = nregions;` before the loop in `mtd_intel_dg.c`, and the commit message explicitly states: "The regions array is counted by nregions, but it's set only after accessing it." The UBSAN error "index 0 is out of range" confirms the array was accessed before its length was set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the nregions field of the nvm structure to the actual number of regions to avoid incorrect region count in subsequent operations.
intent_record.what: Added assignment `nvm->nregions = nregions;` after `mutex_init(&nvm->lock);` and before the loop iterating over regions.
intent_record.how: Ensures the `nvm->nregions` field is set to the value of `nregions` variable, which contains the actual number of regions, so that subsequent code that uses this field (e.g., iteration bounds or checks) operates correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling in intel_dg_mtd_probe to treat memory allocation failure as fatal instead of skipping the region, preventing incomplete region data.
intent_record.what: Changed the error handling in a loop: when kasprintf fails, instead of continuing to the next iteration and skipping the failed allocation, the code now jumps to an error label with ret = -ENOMEM and removes the subsequent assignment of nvm->nregions.
intent_record.how: The probe function now aborts entirely if any region name allocation fails, rather than continuing with potentially missing region names. The nvm->nregions assignment after the loop is removed because the probe will either succeed completely or fail completely.

candidates.rationale: This loop populates the nvm->regions array while nvm->nregions is still uninitialized (zero). Any subsequent code that relies on nregions (e.g., as an array bound) will see an incorrect count, leading to out-of-bounds accesses.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop populates the nvm->regions array while nvm->nregions is still uninitialized (zero). After the loop, nvm->nregions is set, but any code that uses nregions during or after the loop (before it is set) will see an incorrect count, leading to out-of-bounds access. The fix requires moving the initialization of nregions before this loop.
